title: Best interest of the child - how courts actually apply this standard
p1:
A parent winning a custody battle does not always mean the child wins.

Many people assume courts simply choose the parent who is financially stronger, more educated, or more influential. But custody decisions are not popularity contests.
p2:
The surprising part: courts usually do not ask, "Who deserves the child more?" They ask, "What arrangement will protect the child's overall well-being?"

The child's emotional security, relationship with both parents, safety, stability, education, and daily care often matter more than a parent's personal claims.
p3:
The 'best interest of the child' standard means every decision is viewed through the child's needs, not the conflict between adults. A parent with more money may not get preference if another arrangement provides a healthier environment.

The key takeaway: custody is not about rewarding parents. It is about creating the most supportive future for the child.
conclusion: Do you think courts should give more weight to a child's emotional needs or practical factors like financial stability when deciding custody?
